Most heroes are registered with the Hero Association and are divided into four classes with increasing prestige: C-Class, B-Class, A-Class and S-Class. Heroes are given number rankings within their respective classes.

There are numerous unnamed heroes.

entries.name: Unregistered Heroes
entries.content:
Unregistered heroes are often regarded as "weirdos" by the Hero Association and do not get any credits or mentions in any media even some of them are well-respected figures within society like the non-hero-association-affiliated members of Council of Swordmasters. There are currently no known unregistered heroes, however, Saitama and Genos previously did unregistered hero work in the past. Often civilians will do and help heroes with hero work, like when Atomic Samurai asked for the help from the members of the Council of Swordmasters to defeat Garou, or Bomb helped Bang and Genos to fight against Garou, Elder Centipede and other Mysterious Beings from the Monster Association, and later save other defeated heroes.

There are mercenary service that deliver hero-like service for rich clients to protect their assets or do bodyguard works similar to how heroes are dispatched by Hero Associations or Neo Heroes to deal with threats or bodyguarding major sponsors.

entries.name: C-Class Heroes
entries.content: C-Class: The lowest and least strong class out of the four classes. Although C-Class heroes are the weakest, their strength exceeds that of an average person. When a hero enters the association, they normally begin here. C-Class heroes must perform weekly heroic acts to fulfill their quotas, otherwise they are removed from the Hero Registry. The current highest-ranked C-Class hero is Mumen Rider. There are currently 390 heroes in this class, the most numerous out of all the classes.

entries.name: B-Class Heroes
entries.content: B-Class: The third strongest class out of the four classes. When a hero reaches Rank 1 in C-Class, they can climb up to B-Class. Heroes in this class do not have to perform weekly heroic acts to fulfill any quotas, and are also capable of defeating Wolf-level Mysterious Beings by themselves. The current highest-ranked B-Class hero is Fubuki. There were 101 heroes in this class before Saitama's promotion to A-Class.

entries.name: A-Class Heroes
entries.content: A-Class: The second strongest class of the four classes. When a hero reaches Rank 1 in B-Class, they can climb up to A-Class. Heroes in this class are capable of defeating disaster level Tiger Mysterious beings alone and are also considered very popular. The current highest-ranked A-Class hero is Sweet Mask. There were 38 heroes in this class before the Monster Association incident. After said incident, Saitama was promoted to Rank 39 in this class, thus there are currently at least 39 heroes in the class.

entries.name: S-Class Heroes
entries.content: S-Class: The strongest and most prestigious class of the Hero Association. Every hero in the S-Class is equivalent to an emergency army division. This class was originally created to gather individuals who, despite their low ranking, were capable of defeating disaster level Demon Mysterious Beings on their own. The current highest-ranked S-Class hero is Blast. There used to be 17 heroes in this class. Following Silver Fang, and Child Emperor's resignation, there are currently 15 heroes in this class, the lowest amount of members out of all the classes.

entries.name: A-City
entries.content:
A-City was a very large city on Earth. After being completely destroyed by the Dark Matter Thieves, the area was rebuilt by Metal Knight into an expansive complex with highways leading to the other cities. It now serves as the location of the new Hero Association headquarters and is currently inhabited by Hero Association heroes and staff.
Before the Monster Association incident, there were 67 heroes living in this city.

It is later opened as a private residential complex for the rich, complete with pools, restaurants, cafes, and even an underground mall.

entries.name: B-City
entries.content:
B-City is a large city on Earth. This city was briefly seen when The Brain and Brawn Brothers headed there in their quest to rule the world.

There are at least 12 heroes living in this city.

entries.name: Bang's dojo
entries.content:
Bang's dojo is the training facility where Bang teaches Water Stream Rock Smashing Fist. The dojo was passed down to Bang from previous generations.

The dojo is located on top of a mountain in Z-City. There are hundreds of stairs on the path to the dojo and a waterfall starts from said mountain nearby.

entries.name: Boros' Home Planet
entries.content:
Boros's home planet is the planet where Boros was born.

According to Boros himself, the planet has harsh climates, resulting in his species adapting by developing the greatest regenerative abilities in the entire universe.

entries.name: C-City
entries.content:
C-City is a large city on Earth. It consists of a super stadium.
There are at least 16 heroes living in this city.

entries.name: C-City Super Stadium
entries.content:
The C-City Super Stadium is a public stadium in C-City for competitions like the Super Fight Martial Arts Tournament.

This is an oval-shaped arena with a length of several hundred meters, with bleachers and a platform in the center, the entrance to which is equipped with a gate, where both participants and spectators come to pay for admission. Waiting rooms are provided inside the premises for the attention of participants.

Between the bleachers and the tiled area, which acts as a fighting area, there is a lawn on which some spectators can be accommodated. There are changing rooms inside the walls. There is also a toilet in the room.

The stadium was later partially destroyed by Gouketsu.

entries.name: Super Fight Martial Arts Tournament
entries.content:
The Super Fight is a martial arts tournament hosted in the C-City Super Stadium every six months that invites acknowledged dojos to send members to compete.

The Super Fight has been used by some as a way to promote their dojos or their names. There have been 22 tournaments so far. The first Super Fight was highly publicized and had the largest amount of participation as well as broke all records of attendance.

entries.name: Combat Experimentation Room
entries.content:
A large white room hidden under the House of Evolution headquarters, locked away under a metal trapdoor.

Upon entering this room there is a long underground tunnel that leads from the metal trapdoor entrance, all the way to the huge white room.

The combat experimentation room is the largest room in the facility.

entries.name: D-City
entries.content: D-City is a large city on Earth. This city was briefly seen when The Brain and Brawn Brothers demolished some buildings and eventually the whole metropolis. The hero in charge of supervision of the city is the A-Class, Lightning Genji.

entries.name: E-City
entries.content: E-City is a relatively small city situated on Earth. Nothing much is known about this city.

entries.name: E-City Animal Park
entries.content:
E-City Thrill Animal Park is a zoo located in E-City.

This is a regular zoo that exists within E-City, though many herbivores living there transformed into Mysterious Beings for unknown reasons. They soon took over, chasing out all civilians and taking the park for themselves.

Genos and Drive Knight soon swept through the area, killing the monsterized herbivores. The park was significantly damaged by the battle.

entries.name: Earth / World
entries.content:
Earth is the planet on which One-Punch Man takes place. Although the planet largely resembles the real-world Earth, it possesses some distinctive differences.

The Earth, possesses a single super-continent instead of multiple large landmasses. The continent has 26 cities, each identified by a letter of the modern English alphabet.

In addition to the supercontinent covering most of the planet, it possesses smaller islands and landmasses that lie in its immense ocean.

Humans are the dominant species of Earth. The planet is also home to multiple species of plants and animals. Unclassified creatures are grouped into a category of beings called Mysterious Beings / Monsters. This category also includes non-human races, such as the Subterranean People, the Skyfolk, the Seafolk, and the Terror Lizard Clan.

entries.name: F-City
entries.content: F-City is a large city situated on Earth. Not much is known about the location, other than the hero in charge of supervision of the city is the A-Class, Sneck; and that the Paradisers incident happened in and around the central business district. The leader of the Paradisers, Hammerhead, was last spotted in this city.

entries.name: G-City
entries.content: G-City is a large city situated on Earth. It holds the Council of Swordmasters' headquarters.

entries.name: H-City
entries.content: H-City is a large city situated in the north-east on Earth. Not much is known about the location, other than that the heroes in charge of supervision of the city are the B-Class, Mushroom and the C-Class, Horse-Bone

entries.name: Hero Apartment 104 / Saitama's Current Apartment
entries.content: This is Saitama's third apartment. He moved in after his second apartment was destroyed and was promoted to A-Class. He personally requested to have the smallest room in the complex, as he finds it calming. Genos lives separately from Saitama now as it is said to be smaller than the previous apartment. Not much is seen within the apartment, but it's known to be a small box shaped room with furniture and some remains from the old apartment.

entries.name: House of Takoyaki
entries.content: The House of Takoyaki is a takoyaki store run by Dr. Genus with the help of Armored Gorilla. He opened the store because one of his experiments in physical regeneration resulted in infinite growth of octopus tentacles. If you go there you can be greeted by a cute Mosquito Girl working there.

entries.name: I-City
entries.content:
I-City is a large city situated on Earth.
There are at least 14 heroes living in this city.

entries.name: J-City
entries.content:
J-City is a large seaside city situated on the Earth.
There are at least 15 heroes living in this city.

The Evacuation Shelter is a public shelter located in J-City, built by the Hero Association for use in the event of an attack by high-level Mysterious Beings. It was used when the Deep Sea King attacked, although it was broken open. Externally, it consists of a giant dome with circular windows lined around the top.

Smelly Lid Prison is a high-security prison that holds some of the world's most dangerous criminals. It is located on a small island just off the coast of J-City. The S-Class Hero, Puri-Puri Prisoner, is imprisoned in this facility and regularly breaks out to do hero work.

There is also a Junkyard located on the same island as the prison, which is where the monster TV Junkyard Monster was created.

entries.name: K-City
entries.content:
K-City is a city situated on the Earth. It has several forests.
There are 16 heroes living in this city.

entries.name: King's apartment
entries.content:
King's apartment is the primary residence of S-Class hero King.

The apartment is on the 22nd floor of a tall complex. King's apartment is messy and consists of a small kitchen area, a large flat screen TV, game console, coffee table and a shelf with many games, including Doki Doki Sisters. There are also trophies of King in his residence.

entries.name: Kuseno's Laboratory
entries.content: Dr. Kuseno's Scientific Research Facility, where he works his robotic studies. This is also the place Genos usually goes for his repairs and upgrades after battle.

entries.name: L-City
entries.content:
L-City is a large city situated on the Earth. Nothing much is known about this city.
There are 14 heroes living in this city.

entries.name: M-City
entries.content:
M-City is a very large city situated on the Earth.
There are 42 heroes living in this city.

entries.name: Monster Association Headquarters
entries.content:
The Monster Association Headquarters is the hideout and base of operations of the Monster Association. The base is immense, housing over 500 monsters, and leads out to multiple cities through the tunnels created by Elder Centipede.

The Monster Association's base is subterranean in nature, lying deep beneath the Z-City Ghost Town. The Monster Association's presence is a large factor why the ghost town is abandoned. It is largely vertical in shape, almost like an underground tower of sorts, with countless tunnels and staircases connecting its levels. The main hall of the base is Orochi's throne room, where the Association gathers for briefings and other matters. In its maze-like tunnels are other facilities such as prisons, where hostages are held, and mines, where worker monsters mine resources such as gold and jewels. It also has functioning toilets and elevators.

Hidden even further beneath the headquarters, approximately fifteen-hundred meters under the surface, is Psykos' secret chamber. It doubles as her place of rest and a personal laboratory. She claims that no monsters know of its existence. From there she controls her meat puppet Gyoro Gyoro, who in turn leads the entire Monster Association. In order for her psychic waves to reach the rest of the headquarters, Psykos had to install psychic relay points throughout the base.

The Monster Association headquarters is derived from tunnels which were already made by the Subterranean People and the giant centipedes. After the Subterraneans drove themselves to extinction via infighting after the loss of their leader, the Monster Association took the base for themselves, leaving many corpses of the indigenous people buried deep in the base.

entries.name: Moon
entries.content:
The Moon is the Earth's natural satellite.

It originally resembled the moon in real life. During his fight with Boros, Saitama altered the moon's appearance by jumping back to Earth from it, leaving a huge crater on the natural satellite.

Nearly the end of the Monster Association incident, it is revealed that there is another crater on the back of the moon, the other side from where Saitama had made his jump. The crater is much deeper and appears as if it has been dug and not natural at all, with what seems to be a strange spine-like stone peeking out from the center of that hole.

entries.name: N-City
entries.content:
N-City is a large city situated on the Earth. It is east-adjacent to the central A-City.
There are 15 heroes living in this city.

entries.name: Ninja Village
entries.content:
The Ninja Village was a secret institution located deep in the mountains of an unknown place, inaccessible to ordinary people thanks to the barrier the founder put in place around it. Its sole purpose was the training of highly skilled ninja assassins. It is the hometown of Speed-o'-Sound Sonic, Flashy Flash, Hellfire Flame, and Gale Wind. According to Flashy Flash, the village consisted of only males. It was modeled on a mysterious cube.

Ninjas who graduated from the village possess extreme levels of speed and are highly skilled in both martial arts and swordsmanship.

The Abandoned Masses is their direct competitor.

The ninja village was a horrible and utterly despicable place. Children under the age of seven were sent there to train for 10 years, doing nothing but sharpening their assassination skills under extremely ruthless conditions. They were then sold off to factories of the underworld. Escape from the village is virtually impossible, and ninjas may only leave when they complete the curriculum and obtain permission to graduate. A day in the ninja village was 72 hours, with only 6 for sleep. The food was tasteless, and any information from the outside world was completely cut off. Any kind of emotions were not allowed to be expressed, and those who shed their emotions gained excellent ratings. Additionally, companionship and a sense of brotherhood among the classes was not allowed; even talking to others was prohibited. Instructors went so far as to say that if they ever crossed paths in the future after graduating, it was kill or be killed. Flashy Flash described it as a hellish environment. Despite this, many of the ninjas resent Flashy Flash for destroying the village, showing that they still respect it.

The training regimen was extremely arduous. The ninjas were separated into five classes of training based on their skills. Class One was reserved for the most powerful ninjas, and people in this class received the most lenient training, while ninjas in Class Five, the class for the weakest ones, receive the harshest training to boost up their strength.

Hellfire Flame and Gale Wind are the graduates of the 37th class, Golden, and were among the top of that class, while Sonic and Flashy Flash are the sole survivors of the 44th class, with Flash being the No. 1 of the class. Flashy Flash is responsible for the deaths of the 44th Graduation Class and the rest of the entire village, known as The End, and all the ninjas of previous graduating classes regard him as a criminal. The 44th class was rumored to have been failed products because of mistakes made during the training process according to Gale Wind, a fact further enforced by Sonic.

entries.name: Ninja Village History
entries.content:
Sometime in the past, the ninja village was founded by the man regarded as the most powerful ninja to ever walk the earth. From this point on, several ninjas were trained in separate graduating classes and were sent to factories in the underworld to be used as assassins and killing machines. The Ninja Village was in rivalry with the Abandoned Masses but often tried to avoid them due to how dangerous the Masses were.

About 20 years ago, Flashy Flash was sold by his parents at the age of 5 to the Ninja Village. Throughout his childhood, Flashy Flash was consistently pushed to his limits and kept alive through specially formulated medicines. Eventually, he decided to purposefully perform badly in order to receive the harshest training in Class 5. Sometime during his training, he ran across Speed-o'-Sound Sonic, and the two bonded due to both of them being in Class 5. During a mission to dispatch a group of genetically-enhanced beasts as part of their training, Sonic expressed his desire to topple the corrupt administration of the Ninja Village in order to replace it with a more benevolent one and asked Flash to help him in which Flash gladly accepted.

Sometime during this period, the leader of the ninja village challenged Blast and was defeated. Although Blast didn't kill him, the leader was put in a coma, and the ninja village placed him in a regeneration chamber to speed up his healing.

Several years passed, and by the time Flashy Flash was 16, he'd long chosen to stop hiding his abilities and was ranked number one. Unbeknownst to the village, however, was that Flashy Flash had secretly begun to execute his plan of overthrowing the village administration. With his fighting abilities becoming formidable enough, Flashy Flash went on a rampage to fulfill the dream he and Sonic agreed upon, killing the instructors, staff, fellow members of his class, and basically everyone who was a part of the evil village. For some reason, Flashy Flash either could not or chose not to kill the leader of the village, possibly because his location was hidden from Flashy Flash or that the hero thought he would be too powerful to kill, even while in a coma. The only one who survived was Sonic, who had been poisoned by Flashy Flash to save his life from his rampage and thanks to the brutal training he endured being in Class 5 all of his life, he managed to survive.

After the village was destroyed, many ninjas of the previous graduating classes decided to band together and form a group known as the Heavenly Ninja Party. Their main goal is to kill Flashy Flash, who they all hate due to him destroying the village, and to welcome "him" (the leader of the ninja village) as their leader to kill the aging Blast. Once this is done, they plan to go out of hiding and take over the world with their superior ninjutsu skills.

entries.name: O-City
entries.content:
O-City is a large city situated on the Earth. Nothing much is known about this city.
There are 28 heroes living in this city

entries.name: P-City
entries.content:
P-City is a large city situated on the Earth. Nothing much is known about this city.
There are 11 heroes living in this city.

entries.name: Q-City
entries.content:
Q-City is a large city situated on the Earth. Not much is known about the location, other than the hero in charge of supervision of the city is the S-Class, Watchdog Man.

Q-City is labeled as the most dangerous city in terms of number and average disaster level of Mysterious Beings. However, Watchdog Man seems to be keeping the area calm. Civilians clean the monster remains after the battles by Watchdog Man.

There are 13 heroes living in this city.

entries.name: R-City
entries.content:
R-City is a large city situated on the Earth.
There are 14 heroes living in this city.

Major Talent Company: Handsome Castle
The Handsome Castle is a talent company where newcomer celebrities come. Sweet Mask is the main face of the talent agency and the Soda Pop Boys are a group of wanna-be heroes that recently joined the Hero Association.

entries.name: S-City
entries.content:
S-City is a city on Earth.
There are 31 heroes living in this city.

Garou's Hideout: A shack located in the forest in a park where Garou usually rested in after his battles.

Mouse Sushi: Mouse Sushi is a popular sushi restaurant. Saitama, Narinki, Waganma and Bad have all eaten there.

S-City Nature Park: A public nature park in S-City. Garou took shelter in the park in between hunts.[2] The park is incredibly large, even larger than Elder Centipede.

Cafe & Restaurant Togus: The cafe is visited by Garou, Saitama and Fubuki. They serve a variety western food.

entries.name: Shelter Nr. 7
entries.content:
Shelter Nr. 7 is a "fortress for protecting humanity". It is a public shelter located in Z-City, built by the Hero Association spending a vast sum of money, for the event of attack by Mysterious Beings.

Shelter Nr. 7 very much resembles a sporting venue, with at least seven different entrances meant to accommodate large crowds. Externally, it consists of a giant dome lined with circular vents.

The shelter was designed specifically to repel Mysterious Beings. The exterior can withstand super-hot temperatures, and absorb all manner of impacts. Tanks and Missiles are powerless against the shelter's impregnable walls. The main entrance has a biometric identification device that can even detect monsters disguised as humans.

The interior of the shelter is largely open space. Overhead sprinklers were installed to disseminate a negative ion mist, and classical music is played to aid relaxation and relieve the evacuee's stress. Once the shelter's defense system is active, the exit is sealed and locked.

However, Shelter Nr. 7 does not feature any restrooms, a rather glaring oversight given its enormous capacity.

entries.name: Smelly Lid Prison
entries.content:
Smelly Lid Prison / The Stink Slammer is a prison located on a small island off the coast of J-City. This prison holds some of the worst criminals on Earth.

The prison has a tall gate and tall walls with barbed wires. The building is heavily monitored with cameras on different locations with large monitors for the guards to see. For more difficult prisoners like Speed-o'-Sound Sonic, they use a special restraining device designed by the Hero Association. The cells that hold the most difficult prisoners are behind a thick, barricaded door. Inside are the most difficult offenders, who can use their strength to pry open iron bars or use everyday objects as weapons, keys and poison. The inside of the walls are made of steel and there are no windows, and only Puri-Puri Prisoner can break through the walls.

There is a junkyard somewhere outside of the prison, it's said the prison is on an island near J-City.

As part of the Monster Association raid, some prisoners have been transformed into monsters by Nyan. Some prison wardens were also killed in the monster raid.

entries.name: Space
entries.content:
Outer space, or simply space, is the vast and empty area outside Earth's atmosphere. It includes planets, stars, galaxies, and everything in existence of the One-Punch Man universe.

Life beyond Earth exists in the One-Punch Man universe, as proven by the existence of the Dark Matter Thieves, a group of extraterrestrials.

In order to find a worthy opponent that could give him a challenging fight, Lord Boros and the Dark Matter Thieves led by him travelled through space for many years via the giant spaceship. For that reason, Boros was known as the Dominator of the Universe. From an unknown place in the universe, it took Boros and his crew 20 years travelling through space to finally arrive on the planet Earth after speaking to an alien seer.

entries.name: T-City
entries.content:
T-City is a small city situated on the Earth. Nothing much is known about this city.
There are 15 heroes living in this city.[

entries.name: The Mysterious Shrine
entries.content:
A mysterious ancient shrine that is located deep underground. It was found by Orochi. According to him, even Psykos isn't aware of this place.

The area near this shrine is flooded with lava. There are several stone pillars and a staircase which leads to a tablet. On this tablet, there is a depiction of a monster bearing a similar appearance to Orochi being given sacrifices by several humans. There is also an ancient text foretelling the resurrection of a god after a worthy sacrifice is given. However, hidden behind the stone is an image of a larger being and the actual "God" the text spoke of.

The shrine was found by Orochi after he began venturing further into deep underground in an attempt to grow stronger by draining energy directly from the deepest parts of the Earth.

When Orochi approached the shrine, he discovered a tablet which depicted him and stated that a worthy sacrifice was needed in order to resurrect "God", leading him to believe that it was referring to him as a god. From that point onwards, the Monster King always searched for a "worthy sacrifice" that was required for his resurrection as a god according to the tablet until he met Saitama.

entries.name: U-City
entries.content:
U-City is a very large city situated on the Earth. Nothing much is known about this city.
There are 30 heroes living in this city.

entries.name: V-City
entries.content:
V-City is a large city situated on the Earth.
There are 16 heroes living in this city.

entries.name: W-City
entries.content:
W-City is a large city on Earth. The A-Class hero Heavy Kong is the hero in charge of watching this city.
There are 14 heroes in this city.[

entries.name: X-City
entries.content:
X-City is a large city situated on the Earth. Nothing much is known about this city.
There are 13 heroes in this city.

entries.name: Y-City
entries.content:
Y-City is a large city on Earth. Child Emperor's Lab is located in this city.
There are 14 heroes living in this city.

Child Emperor's Laboratory: A laboratory owned by Child Emperor is located in Y-City. He builds and experiments with various gadgets here. He is seen sitting on his movable chair.

Restaurant Mammoth: A gourmet restaurant where Fubuki brought Saitama, Genos and King (it is unknown if Bang came too). It seems to have quite a large menu, which includes; Salads with dressing, sirloin, fillet and butter topping.

entries.name: Z-City Ghost Town
entries.content:
The Z-City Ghost Town is a large uninhabited neighborhood located on the east side of Z-City.

When cases of high-level monsters appearing in the neighborhood increased all of a sudden in the last few years, all citizens supposedly moved in masses to the center. As a result, the whole neighborhood was deserted and it's now a ghost town, but with the critical infrastructure like electricity and water supply intact.

Among the normal citizens of Earth, it's just supposed to simply be some abandoned ruins on the outskirts of Z-City.

entries.name: Z-City
entries.content:
Z-City is a large city on Earth. It consists of a business district, a residential district, and an abandoned, trashed area commonly referred to as the Ghost Town. Saitama and Genos are inhabitants of the latter area, which is home to many Mysterious Beings but is free to live in. It is rumored to contain incredibly powerful Mysterious Beings.

Z-City has had the greatest percentage increase of monster appearances in the past decade.

There are at least 4 heroes living in this city.

entries.name: Psykorochi
entries.content:
Having barely survived his battle with Saitama, Orochi uses his absorption ability to regenerate his body. He absorbs his master Psykos; however, Psykos resists complete assimilation and the two merge into one. During the fusion, they met and received additional power from a being they refer to as God. They are strong enough to injure Tatsumaki and force her to get serious. Their destructive capacity also immensely increases, capable of creating tsunamis over a portion of the planet's hemisphere with a single attack.

Through their union and subsequent powerup by "God", Orochi in his fused form has the potential to corrupt, supplant and assimilate living & non-biological matter through his cellular mass-based biology. This can enable the amalgam to spread out and consume the world, becoming a mind capable of giving automation to the whole of the Earth, essentially becoming a living planet.

entries.name: Webigaza
entries.content:
Webigaza is a former idol singer who currently works as a leader in the Neo Heroes organization.

Webigaza is an attractive young girl with large, bright eyes and long, light-colored hair. She has blunt bangs that frame her forehead, and her hair is embellished with accessories like headbands and beads or chains. Underneath a frilly dress, she dons a Neo Heroes battle suit. When she activates her power during combat, a pair of wings appear behind her and tendrils of lightning appear intermittently around her body.

Being a pop star, Webigaza is a charismatic woman, appealing to her legions of fans. She is very determined, having a desire to surpass the idol and hero Sweet Mask to the point of jealousy, even taking a break from her own life as a celebrity to undergo cybernetic and physical enhancement. She also has a hotheaded side, angrily hitting a wall and causing it to crack upon her knowledge that Sweet Mask had turned into a monster and subsequently gone missing. Due to being exploited and betrayed throughout her career, she is naturally untrusting of others, though willing to open up to some people such as Child Emperor. Her obsession with power led her to depend on the Neo Heroes' technology to survive, a decision she has become content with, regardless of what future consequences it might cause for her. She seems to be a friendly person, as evidenced by her conversation with Child Emperor.

As a Neo Leader, Webigaza is a very powerful hero. After having her body modified, her strength increases several-fold. Solitude, a Neo Heroes Leader candidate, is startled by her strength and the fact that she managed to survive having 71% of her body modified, a very risky and usually unsuccessful process.

entries.name: Empty Void
entries.content:
Empty Void, who now goes by the alias That Ma, is the founder of the secret Ninja Village.

Void used to be Blast's partner during his search for the mysterious cubes. After becoming influenced by "God", he monsterized and became a Mysterious Being.

As a human, Void was lean but muscular. He had light-coloured long rough hair, which he tied in a ponytail. He wore goggles and a scarf, modern body armor, and a utility belt. He has a more slender build but is around the same height as Blast. His light-colored hair is cut similarly to Blast apart from towards the back where it forms into a long ponytail. He wears multiple pieces of armor on his arms, shoulders, chest, and back. Underneath, he wears all-black attire including his gloves, and has multiple pieces of cloth wrapped around his torso. His two sheathed katanas are attached to his back and he has what appears to be small pouches held in place on the back of his waist.

As a monster, Void has a monstrous appearance with spiked skin and flamed hair. He has different skin colors on different parts of his body. His teeth are all razor-sharp. Initially depicted as having a skinny and emaciated physique, likely due to past injuries inflicted by Blast, Void undergoes a substantial transformation upon absorbing divine power from Garou, becoming muscular and robust.

As Blast's partner, Void was probably a good person before becoming a Mysterious Being.

As the leader of the Ninja Village, Void is an extremely powerful individual. He fought Blast, the top-ranking S-Class hero, and was defeated even after gaining the power from monsterization. According to Blast, the two were on par with each other, but after gaining additional powers from "God", Void gained a big advantage in the fight. Despite this, however, Blast was still somehow able to defeat and leave him gravely injured.

After Garou's defeat by Saitama which caused the former's divine power to escape him, Void covertly absorbed the entirety of that leaked divine energy to revitalize himself from a weakened state to a significantly improved condition. This absorption of power heals him from injuries sustained during his battle with Blast 15 years ago, which left him weakened. Blast remarks that he has not only healed but also grown stronger as a result of this absorption. When discussing this incident with Sitch, Blast asserts that Void now poses an even greater threat than the Hero Hunter.

Immense Speed and Reflexes: Void possesses an astounding level of speed and reflexes, placing him among the fastest individuals demonstrated in the series. His supreme mastery over ninjutsu grants him heightened swiftness and agility. For instance, he could effortlessly outmaneuver Flashy Flash, an S-Class hero known for his own extraordinary speed. Furthermore, Void has proven capable of keeping up with Blast, the top-ranking S-Class hero, who is exceptionally fast and agile in combat.

Immense Strength: Void possesses considerable physical strength, being able to effortlessly carry a mysterious cube in his hand while fighting Flashy Flash. Said cube is so heavy that it sinks into solid rock.

Vacuum Endurance: Void has demonstrated the ability to remain suspended in space without suffering adverse effects. This suggests that he can survive in the vacuum of space at least for a certain duration.

Transformation: Void can transform his appearance. After absorbing Garou's divine power, he underwent a significant change in appearance - he grew long hair and donned a mask, likely as a visual representation of the power he had gained. However, when confronting Speed-o'-Sound Sonic and Flashy Flash, he had already reverted to his previous appearance, presumably to conserve his energy.

Dimensional Travel: Much like Blast, Void has the ability to traverse between dimensions.

Energy Absorption: Void possesses the ability to absorb energy from others. Following Saitama's defeat of Garou, Void absorbed the divine energy emanating from Garou's body, which not only revitalized him from a weakened state to a vastly improved condition but also elevated his abilities to a significant extent, enabling him to fend off a few assaults from Blast shortly after.

Illusion Inducement: Void can generate illusions that disorient the senses of his targets, facilitating easier attacks. He used this ability to confuse Speed-o'-Sound Sonic and catch him off-guard by making the ninja perceive him as Flashy Flash.

Spatial Bending: Similar to Blast, Void possesses the ability to manipulate space to some extent. With his bare hands, he can interact with and grab the fabric of space around him like a blanket, using it to hide himself and vanish from sight.

Parallel Viewing: "God" granted Void the ability to access a hyperspace outside of the causality of the universe, where he can perceive parallel worlds infinitely branching out with every possibility. These parallel universes and alternate realities are visually represented to him as floating "bubbles" that he can observe and interact with. This ability potentially gives him insight into different timelines and variations of reality. It is also the underlying mechanism by which he utilizes his Dimensional Slash technique.

Ninjutsu Master: Being considered the strongest ninja to have ever lived, Void possesses great mastery over ninjutsu. He is proficient in the use of an absurd variety of weapons, and carries them into battle.

Dimensional Slash: A formidable technique bestowed upon Void by "God" that involves interference from a higher dimension. When used, he enters a hyperspace dimension or plane of existence beyond the causality of the universe, where he can perceive endless floating "bubbles" representing parallel worlds and their possibilities, which he interacts with using a special jutsu. After choosing a specific one, Void pinpoints the target of his attack before slicing through the selected bubble in order to unleash interdimensional slashes that manifest at the target's exact location from outside the universe; its effectiveness, however, depends on the user's capabilities. During its first use, Void unleashed widespread, devastating slashes from this higher plane aimed at the Hero Association headquarters, splitting the surface and creating deep holes in the ground. This attack would also have most certainly destroyed the headquarters had Blast not teleported the building away.

Swords: Void carries two swords on his back.

Mysterious Cube: Void keeps a mysterious cube in his possession. By either inducing someone to make physical contact with the cube, or forcibly pressing it against them, he can trigger its ability to immediately render them unconscious for a temporary duration. While unconscious, the victim experiences a vision or dream in which they encounter "God," who offers them power. He attempted to convert Sonic and Flash into Mysterious Beings using this method.

entries.name: Great Giant Anteater
entries.content: A disaster level tiger monster. It's grown too huge and seeks new food to replace ants. He was killed by Suiryu.

entries.name: Emperor Giant Anteater
entries.content: A disaster level demon monster who was similar to Emperor Giant Anteater but stronger. It was killed by Webigaza.

entries.name: Neo Heroes History / Structure
entries.content:
Unlike the Hero Association, which selects heroes through a physical and written test, the Neo Heroes recruit members through a special headhunting system. There are more than 2000 candidates within the Neo Heroes ranks which far exceeds the 546 pro heroes of the Hero Association. Due to the counterproductive and anti-meritocratic nature of the ranking system at Hero Association, the Neo Heroes eschews such practices in favor of attempting to create a culture where strong and weak heroes can work together and support each other. Furthermore, the organization seems to know the shortcomings of the current Hero Association in terms of misconduct, unfair treatment of its superhumans and collateral damage often caused by their more powerful heroes, such as Tatsumaki. They keep this criticism in mind and attempt to minimize such shortcomings in their own organization, a willingness to change the way heroes operate is the main cause of Child Emperor's defection from the Hero Association and join this new hero organization.

The Neo Heroes have recruited a handful of S-Class heroes to join their organization, including Metal Bat, Child Emperor and Superalloy Darkshine; in a talent scouting bid to outpace their neighboring counterparts in the Hero Association. According to the Neo Heroes' recruiter, they promise to treat their heroes much fairer than the premiere hero agency. With the Neo Heroes offering multiple membership benefits that entice many up and comers or veteran do-gooders to join their organization. Enticements ranging from novelties such as clothing, increased income, room and board as well as familial benefits on top of an abundance in hero equipment even for new or lower-ranking supers. Their willingness to meet the needs of their operatives caused the former S-Class hero Metal Bat to join them. Unlike the Hero Association, the Neo Heroes are more focused on the safety of heroes working under them, forgoing the forced quotas to maintain their hero rank. They do, however, require that their heroes possess a "normative awareness," despite this the organization took no issue with Raiden attacking Superalloy Darkshine despite the latter's clear discomfort with engaging in combat. They also raised no qualms with two top-position candidates attacking other heroes to prove a point, showing that the bullying culture between strong and weak heroes still remains to an extent.

Their method of talent searching was once as biased as the conventional test in the Hero Association since they mostly focused on recruiting top tier heroes, indicating why they didn't try to recruit Saitama. However, this attitude has recently changed, as multiple lower-ranked heroes have been invited to join the association, such as the A-Class heroes Forte, Butterfly DX, and Chain'n'toad, as well as the group containing two C-Class heroes, Soda Pop Boys. This arrangement also has a dark side in which they recruit highly controversial members like serial killers, racketeers and cult leaders; such as the likes of A and Infelsinave based on the merit of combat prowess and for social following rather than any inherent desire for justice. This fact makes Speed-o'-Sound Sonic state that the Neo Heroes are even more "rotten" than the criminal underworld.

Recently, Child Emperor and Metal Bat had discovered the more sinister sides of the Neo Hero establishment. A dark underbelly that not even Blue is aware of, case in point being that the Neo Heroes possesses a cybernization program dubbed as a recovery and performance-enhancing operation for heavily injured Neo Heroes members to heal them and enhance their performance through cybernetic enhancements. The process of which is purposely invalidated as to keep employees within their service, as those whom're enhanced this way become dependent upon constant maintenance which only the organization can provide for their bionic augmentations. Darkshine too came under suspicion while training some new requites within their gymnasium as the operation feeds Neo Hero candidates a special energy drink that causes the taker to develop increased muscle mass and other physical dynamics at incredible rates; but at the cost of making them increasingly aggressive to the point of violent outburst and overconfidence. During the encounter between the hedonistic killer and Sonic, A reveals that the Neo Heroes are actively on the hunt for strong advocates in the cyborgification initiative. Seeking out powerful individuals regardless of moral alignment to turn them into cyborg puppets even outside organization purviews as A, among other Neo Leaders, is tasked with capturing Sonic with such intent. Child Emperor also suspects that a lot of monsters are actually controlled by the Neo Hero sect as he discovered microchips within the base of brains belonging to many dead Dragon-Level threats that they were tasked to dispatch recently.

Other issues with the new hero group being their rather belligerent interactions with their senior predecessors within the Hero Association. Mainly stemming from how the Neo Heroes went after some of the Hero Association's more prominent enforcers while blatantly disregarding any attempt by the latter to establish proper relations to join forces in the future. Something which is highlighted with Ryumon's merit stealing with Crescent Eyebroll against a monster threat too tough for him to handle alone. A trait which even Black Sperm found more detrimental than beneficial to both orders in the long run, for instead of working together they spend more time sniping at one another thus weakening the efficacy of both organizations and humanity as a whole. Citing it as a temporary fix to the problems in society while making the prim and proper Neo Heroes less capable of dealing with the more major assaults from monsters and calamities down the line.

During the meeting between Blue and Forte, Forte reveals that the Neo Heroes operation methods actually hamper the growth of individual heroes by making them depend too much on their battle suits.

Not to mention their extreme emphasis on efficiency, leaving little to no room for advancement in personal strength of the individual since singular heroes never have to put all on the line in life or death situations to radically improve themselves. Furthermore, because almost no Neo Hero members actually constantly put risking anything as much as heroes from the Hero Association, they often lack charisma as an individual since the public only refers to the organization as a whole and rarely remembers them by their name, even Neo Leaders.
